overview.summary: String Quartet op. 18 no. 1 — Movement 1 belongs to the Early Romantic era — music by Ludwig van Beethoven.
overview.history: String Quartet op. 18 no. 1 — Movement 1 is ready to explore on Lune. It is associated with Ludwig van Beethoven. Stylistically it sits in the Early Romantic world. Start by listening, then ask about the bars that surprise your hands. Place every phrase in the Early Romantic sound-world: how would someone from that time shape it?

eraInfo.label: Early Romantic
eraInfo.story: Personal feeling steps forward. Rubato, dramatic contrasts, and singing melodies on the piano become part of the language.
tips: Balance heart with a steady left hand.

composerInfo.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
composerInfo.hook: Beethoven stretched classical clarity into stormy personal drama.
composerInfo.bio: Regarded as one of the greatest composers in the history of Western music, he was mentored during the Classical period, and his musical style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music, and the expansion of instrumental forms such as the symphony, the piano sonata and the string quartet. His compositions have attracted extraordinary casual and scholarly interest, and remain among the most performed in the world.
composerInfo.full: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer, conductor, and pianist. Regarded as one of the greatest composers in the history of Western music, he was mentored during the Classical period, and his musical style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music, and the expansion of instrumental forms such as the symphony, the piano sonata and the string quartet. His compositions have attracted extraordinary casual and scholarly interest, and remain among the most performed in the world.
highlights: Beethoven is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

chapters.title: About Ludwig van Beethoven
chapters.body: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer, conductor, and pianist. Regarded as one of the greatest composers in the history of Western music, he was mentored during the Classical period, and his musical style was a key driver of the transition to Romantic music, and the expansion of instrumental forms such as the symphony, the piano sonata and the string quartet. His compositions have attracted extraordinary casual and scholarly interest, and remain among the most performed in the world.
